headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 16 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: Into the last week of La Vuelta 26! Six stages remain on the way to Granada, with a couple of mountain showdowns, the ITT, and three flatter stages that should see baroudeurs and sprinteurs battle it out for the win. Today is the first of these: the 181.1 km route from Cortegana to La Rabida includes 2,250 metres of elevation gain, but that mostly comes from the rolling terrain in the first half of the stage, ahead of a flat run-in to the finish. There are no categorised climbs. The neutral start is set at 13:05, the start proper at 13:18 after a 4.6 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: Welcome to Huelva
subtext: Both Cortegana and La Rabida make their debut as La Vuelta stage towns*. The stage is entirely set in the province of Huelva, previously visited by La Vuelta in 1997 and 2022. On the last occasion, stage 17 started from Aracena (km 31.4 on today’s route) and headed to the Monasterio de Tentudia (in the province of Badajoz). The breakaway made it to the finish, with Rigoberto Uran taking victory (3rd place for Jesus Herrada). Primoz Roglic did not start after the crashed in the final in Tomares the day before. The province of Huelva has also hosted local events such as the Vuelta a Andalucia. *The full list of new stage towns in this edition: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio (15), Cortegana (16), La Rábida (16), Dos Hermanas (17), El Puerto de Santa María (18), La Calahorra (20), and Collado del Aguacil (20).

headline: A decisive final week?
subtext: In the last 25 editions of La Vuelta (2001 - 2025), the overall leader at the beginning of the second week has won the event on 16 occasions. It was the case with Jonas Vingegaard last year. Nine editions saw a rider take the lead in the final week and eventually triumph. Primoz Roglic was the last to do it, taking La Roja from Ben O’Connor on stage 19 of La Vuelta 24. This week offers several opportunities to shake the race, most notably with the individual time trial to Jerez de la Frontera (stage 18) and the two mountains showdowns on days 19 and 20. All in all, the six stages in the final week of La Vuelta 26 add up to: - 907.8 km of racing - 13,716 metres of elevation gain - 270 points for the green jersey - 53 points for the polka-dot jersey.

headline: Grand Tour success at the eleventh hour?
subtext: The third week of La Vuelta brings the final six opportunities to take a Grand Tour stage win in 2026. So far, 32 riders from 17 teams and representing 15 nations have won Grand Tour stages this year. The best scorers: 8 stage wins - Tadej Pogacar 5 - Jonas Vingegaard 3 - Matthew Brennan, Paul Magnier, Tim Merlier, Jhonatan Narvaez 2 - Wout van Aert, Richard Carapaz, Remco Evenepoel, Mathieu van der Poel 1 - Igor Arrieta, Davide Ballerini, Alberto Bettiol, Marco Brenner, Bryan Coquard, Fredrik Dversnes, Filippo Ganna, Olav Kooij, Sepp Kuss, Andreas Leknessund, Enric Mas, Jonathan Milan, Jakob Omrzel, Mads Pedersen, Jasper Philipsen, Mauro Schmid, Alec Segaert, Thomas Silva, Isaac del Toro, Bastien Tronchon, Michael Valgren, Soren Wærenskjold By teams: 13 - UAE Emirates XRG 12 - Visma-Lease a Bike 6 - Soudal Quick-Step 3 - Alpecin-Premier Tech, EF Education-EasyPost, Uno-X Mobility, XDS Astana 2 - Bahrain Victorious, Lidl-Trek, Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe 1 - Cofidis, Decathlon CMA CGM, Groupama-FDJ United, Jayco AlUla, Movistar, Netcompany Ineos, Tudor By nations: 9 - Belgium, Slovenia 7 - Denmark 5 - Ecuador, France 4 - Italy, Netherlands 3 - Great Britain, Norway 2 - Spain 1 - Germany, Mexico, Switzerland, Uruguay, USA

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with a 4.6 km parade.

headline: La Roja
subtext: Last week, Enric Mas (Movistar) did more than defend his overall lead. After his victory at Alto de Aitana (stage 9), the Spanish climber had a margin of 1’18’’ on Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) and there were five more chasers within four minutes of La Roja. Now, Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) is second (+2’06’’), just ahead of Primoz Roglic (+2’10’’), and the gap to Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) in fourth position is up to 4’24’’.

headline: Green jersey
subtext: With his his stage wins in Loja and Cordoba, Wout van Aert significantly increased his lead in the points standings. The Belgian star is up to 267; his Visma-Lease a Bike teammate Matthew Brennan follows with 159 points. Third on stage 15, Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) is up to 153 points. A rider can grab a maximum of 270 points in the final week, including 50 today (30 at the finish, 20 at the intermediate sprint).

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) enters the final week with 69 points in the mountains standings, a tally that gives him a significant margin on Wout van Aert (40 points). Enric Mas (Movistar) follows with 24 points. There are 53 points up for grabs this week, but they’re all packed in stages 19 (20 points) and 20 (33 points).

headline: White jersey
subtext: Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) is still 30’’ ahead of Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) while Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) now trails by 10’41’’.

headline: Team standings
subtext: Decathlon CMA CGM are strong leaders of the overall team standings with a gap of 57’32’’ to XDS Astana and 1h11’15’’ to Bahrain Victorious.

headline: Combativity award
subtext: Among the most active rider in the breakaway son La Vuelta 26, Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X) will race with a distinctive bib as he was named the most combative rider yesterday.

headline: Stage 16 is ON!
subtext: There are 150 riders in the peloton at the beginning of the third and final week of La Vuelta 26.

headline: A fast start
subtext: The bunch is stretched at km 3.

headline: 8 riders on the move
subtext: They've opened a small gap at km 7.

headline: Back together at km 8
subtext: The pace is very intense. Riders like Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United) said at the start today is likely to be their "last chance" in La Vuelta 26.

headline: Paleni: "We'll have to beat the peloton with a strong group, a good strategy and careful management"
subtext: Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United) hinted at a hard battle today: “This is the last chance for riders like me. Tomorrow will be flatter, then there’s the time trial, two mountain stages and the finish. Today’s stage suits me, so I’m going to give it my all. The finish isn’t as tough. There are fewer hills, so we’ll have to beat the peloton in a sprint, with a strong group, a good strategy and careful management throughout the day to try and finish ahead of the peloton. Unfortunately, there’ll be a headwind during the day, which could put the breakaway at a disadvantage, but we’ll see what we can do. First of all, we need to be at the front.”

headline: 5 riders on the move
subtext: As the road rises, a handful of attackers manage to open a small gap. They're at km 14.

headline: The 5 leaders: Vermaerke, Madouas, Dalby...
subtext: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Valentin Madouas (Groupama-FDJ United), Simon Dalby (Uno-X Mobility), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla) and Roland Thalmann (Tudor) are 15'' ahead of the bunch at km 15.

headline: The attackers get away
subtext: The gap has increased to 1'10''.

headline: 20 kilometres of battle
subtext: The gap slightly increases: 1'25''.

headline: Visma-Lease a Bike at the front of the bunch
subtext: "We’ve made a good plan, we’ll try to execute that plan as best as possible, and we have to be happy with that", Matthew Brennan said at the start. The last gap: 1'40'' at km 22.

headline: 2 minutes
subtext: At km 28, the peloton trail by 2'14''.

headline: Thalmann wanted to "stee some action today", so he made the break
subtext: Into the final week of his first Grand Tour, Roland Thalmann (Tudor) found the strength to make today's breakaway. “The fatigue is definitely there", the Swiss rider said at the start. "The first week you feel more and more tired but now it’s more stable, sometimes you can recover a bit like yesterday, or with Sunday’s stage that was not too long. Of course we have the heat that makes it not easy, but I still enjoy it and we almost see Granada coming." "[Marco Brenner’s victory] was an absolutely amazing day for Marco and the team, it gives wings to everybody. We just enjoy the moment, of course we have big ambitions for this week and we want to continue like this, but it gives us a boost." "It could be [a day for the breakaway] but we need a lot of teams with the same idea. Two or three teams definitely want to have a sprint, but if there is a big fight for the breakaway in the start and a good breakaway, in the third week you never know what can happen. Also with the heat and the first part of the race that is not easy. Let’s see, we hope to not have only a calm stage with a sprint, we hope we will see some action today."

headline: Meanwhile in the peloton...
subtext: Jorge Arcas (Movistar) takes care of his leader Enric Mas: “I hope the future will be red. We’ve got six tough days of racing ahead of us. The whole team is fighting tooth and nail alongside Enric and we’re going to try to defend this lead. Today, my job is to support Enric as best I can for as long as possible, making sure he has everything he needs. I’ll make sure he faces as little headwind as possible so that he’s in top form for the tough days ahead, and above all, I’ll look after him very carefully. Enric is calm, but ultimately we know that these so-called ‘transition’ stages are very tricky. We’ve seen plenty of crashes and mishaps involving leaders like Pogacar. Ultimately, I think today is a very important day, just as much as the ones to come.”

headline: 48 km covered in the first hour
subtext: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Valentin Madouas (Groupama-FDJ United), Simon Dalby (Uno-X Mobility), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla) and Roland Thalmann (Tudor) have been racing really hard to open a gap of 2'40''.

headline: The bunch accelerates and splits
subtext: The gap to the five leaders is down to 2'10'' at km 54. The wind blows at around 15 km/h from the west while the race is heading south.

headline: Visma | Lease a Bike control the pace
The two bunches get back together
subtext: The attackers' lead is back up to 2'20''.

headline: The situation settles in the bunch
subtext: And the gap to the breakaway stablises at 2'10''.

headline: The lowest finish of La Vuelta 26
subtext: At 8 metres above sea level, the finish in La Rabida is the lowest of La Vuelta 26, slightly below the 10 metres of altitude in Monaco (stage 1), Xeraco (stage 8) and Sevilla (stage 17). On the other hand, Calar Alto (stage 12) was the highest finish of La Vuelta 26, at 2,153 metres of altitude.

headline: The peloton accelerates again
subtext: And the gap decreases: 1'58''.

headline: 100 kilometres to go
subtext: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Valentin Madouas (Groupama-FDJ United), Simon Dalby (Uno-X Mobility), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla) and Roland Thalmann (Tudor) are still 2 minutes ahead of the bunch.

headline: Brennan eyes "two opportunities coming up"
subtext: Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) spoke about his ambitions at the start: “Not too sure [what my legs tell me before the last week of racing], actually. I feel okay, so I will make a conclusion when I step on the bike and the breakaway formation is happening. Yes, there’s two opportunities coming up. We have a strong team to support that, so we will give our best shot. [We do] not necessarily [feel more pressure after winning 5 stages], we do what we need to do. Personally, I’ve won three stages, Wout [van Aert] has won two… We ticked off our goal of stage winning, so we just have to accept what happens. We’ve made a good plan, we’ll try to execute that plan as best as possible, and we have to be happy with that.”

headline: Visma-Lease a Bike set a strong pace on an uphill section
subtext: Jorgen Nordhagen and Steven Kruijswijk take turns with Bruno Armirail ontheir wheel. The give leaders are 96 km from the finish with a gap down to 1'27''.

headline: The average speed after 2 hours: 45.0 km/h
subtext: The last gap: 1'30''.

headline: Timo Roosen withdraws from La Vuelta 26
subtext: There are 149 riders still in the race.

headline: Meeus: "I think the finale suits me quite well"
subtext: Jordi Meeus (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) already has three podiums in this Vuelta, but no victory: "I feel quite close [to victory], sometimes closer than others, for example the first sprint Brennan was far ahead and not losing speed so there I was quite far, but the other sprints I feel I was pretty close, so today is a new chance. I think Brennan has shown he survives the climbs very well so I have to put a bit more energy into that, I expect him to be at a very good level. It’s true Laporte is gone and that could be to our advantage, but we will see how the final develops. It’s a long straight line towards 1,4 km to go, then a tricky roundabout that will not be at super high speed, then another left bend with 600 meters to go, and then 600 meters straight. I think it suits me quite well."

headline: 80 kilometres to go
subtext: The gap has slighlty increased again: 1'45''.

headline: For the safety of riders and fans
The gap decreases again
subtext: The peloton reach km 106 with a gap of 1'28''. Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike) is setting the pace at the moment.

headline: Nys: "I can be happy"
subtext: Thibau Nys (Lidl-Trek) was 3rd on stage 15, his first top3 in a Grand Tour: "It’s a bit of mixed feeling. I would have loved to win the stage, of course, but I think I can be happy with my shape and with my performance. We try to make the best out of every stage that is coming now and try to optimise our chances. I think [it will be difficult to repeat the same scenario], I think the stages that are coming are either way too hard or not hard enough for me. Maybe the last day in Granada could be a nice opportunity."

headline: Results of the intermediate sprint (Villarrasa, km 114.5)
subtext: 1. Vermaerke, 20 pts / 6'' 2. Sütterlin, 17 pts / 4'' 3. Thalmann, 15 pts / 2'' 4. Madouas, 13 pts 5. Dalby, 10 pts

headline: 60 kilometres to go
subtext: The peloton trail by 1'05''.

headline: Will Romele give it another go? "Today, tomorrow and the day after until the end"
subtext: Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana): "To be fair, the only thing of the rest day was to find a good ice cream to recover a bit. We also had good coffee so it's good. Obviously I looked also the finish [of Sunday, when he was 2nd in Cordoba] but it was my best, I'm super happy for the second place. [Ice cream] is a kind of way to have a good after, I was used to eat ice cream before the important races when I was a junior, so it was a kind of 'good luck' for me and we'll se in the next days to find some ice cream from the team. As I said in the first day, we're gonna try today, tomorrow and the day after until the end of the Vuelta."

headline: 40 seconds with 55 km to go
subtext: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Valentin Madouas (Groupama-FDJ United), Simon Dalby (Uno-X Mobility), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla) and Roland Thalmann (Tudor) face a very hard challenge as they try to hold off the peloton en route to La Rabida.

headline: New faces at the front of the bunch
subtext: Bryan Coquard's Cofidis and Jordi Meeus's Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe take turns with Matthew Brennan's Visma-Lease a Bike to drive the chase. The gap isnow under 40 seconds with just over 50 kilometres to go.

headline: The average speed after 3 hours: 45.6 km/h
subtext: The early attackers have been pushing hard, but the peloton are 39 seconds behind them with 43 km remaining.

headline: The five brave men of the day
A gap of 25 seconds with 40 kilometres to go
subtext: Visma-Lease a Bike, Cofidis and Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe set the pace in the bunch.

headline: Dainese: "My shape improves in the last week"
subtext: Alberto Dainese (Soudal Quick-Step) already won in the last week of the Giro and La Vuelta: "Let's hope [I can repeat it], let's see if today or tomorrow. In general my shape improves in the last week, or maybe the other guys are more tired. I also feel the legs are a bit different in the last week than in the first days. The peloton is smaller and tired, there is less lead-out, in general I just like it. Let’s see today, I think it’s the first sprint [stage] that is totally flat in the last hours, that’s something I like. Today and tomorrow are the last chances for me, so let’s see.”

headline: 30 kilometres to go
subtext: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Valentin Madouas (Groupama-FDJ United), Simon Dalby (Uno-X Mobility), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla) and Roland Thalmann (Tudor) hold to an 18'' gap to the bunch.

headline: The situation settles ahead of the final rush
subtext: The peloton are 12'' behind the five leaders with 25 km to go.

headline: Ivo Oliveira has crashed
subtext: The Portuguese rider from UAE Emirates XRG is back on his feet but he seems in pain.

headline: The pace and the tension increase
subtext: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Valentin Madouas (Groupama-FDJ United), Simon Dalby (Uno-X Mobility), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla) and Roland Thalmann (Tudor) are reeled in with 23.5 km to go.

headline: Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe set a hard pace
subtext: Enric Mas (Movistar) is well positioned behind Primoz Roglic's teammates.

headline: Flying into the final 20 kilometres
subtext: A group of stragglers trail by 30 secodns.

headline: The 6th sprint of La Vuelta 26?
subtext: Stage 2: Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) wins in Manosque Stage 5: Brennan in Roquetes Stage 8: Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) in Xeraco Stage 10: Bastien Tronchon (Groupama-FDJ United) in Elche de la Sierra Stage 11: Brennan in Lorca Stage 16: ?

headline: Uno-X Mobility pulls the second bunch
subtext: Magnus Cort was caught behind. But they're getting closer to the first bunch.

headline: The stragglers get back to the bunch
subtext: They close the gap just as the race enters the final 10 kilometres.

headline: The final 5 kilometres
subtext: Several trains occupy the front positions of the peloton on wide roads.

headline: A battle of trains
subtext: Uno-X Mobility move up to the front of the bunch with 3 kilometres to go. Enric Mas (Movistar) is well positioned.

headline: Last kilometre
subtext: Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step) leads the bunch.

headline: Matthew Brennan wins stages 16 of La Vuelta 26!
subtext: He becomes the first rider to win four stages in his maiden Grand Tour since Fernando Gaviria in the Giro 2017!

headline: Top 5
subtext: 1. Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) 2. Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) 3. Vito Braet (Lotto Intermarché) 4. Jordi Meeus (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) 5. Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility)
